[db=live]Welcome to the Beast Mastery Hunter rotation guide for Midnight Season 2! This guide will teach you all about the optimal rotation for Beast Mastery Hunter across its various talent builds. It will cover both core ability cadence and cooldown usage in dungeons and raids for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b].

sections.heading: How to Play Beast Mastery
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Beast Mastery"][color=c3]Beast Mastery Hunter Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
[color=hunter]Beats Mastery Hunter[/color] generates most of its resources passively, either through passive focus regeneration or through your abilities coming off cooldown. Your goal is to spend your focus wisely while optimizing the cooldowns of your abilities effectively. The current design of the spec is also heavily based around your main cooldown, so optimizing the amount of powerful abilities in your cooldown window is important. 

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_druid_ferociousbite size=medium type=round color=c3 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c3]Optimize your cooldown window[/color][/b] Make sure your [spell=19574] is used on cooldown as often as possible and that you take full advantage of all the resources it gives you, such as [spell=472741], [spell=1264290] and [spell=466990].
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_hunter_killcommand size=medium type=round color=c3 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c3]Maximize your Kill Commands :[/color][/b] You want to make sure that [spell=34026] never reaches two charges, that they're always buffed by [spell=1273126], and that you are able to cast as many of them as possible during your cooldown window.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_hunter_pet_wolf size=medium type=round color=c3 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c3]Manage your pets:[/color][/b] Make sure your pets are always attacking the correct target and that you are effectively moving them when necessary and swapping when you want them to, ideally using [spell=61684].[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]
[center][cta-button guide=32574 icon=ability_hunter_bestialdiscipline]Beast Mastery Hunter Starter Guide[/cta-button][/center]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=ability_hunter_bestialdiscipline type=round size=medium inline=true color=c3][/icon] Best Beast Mastery Hunter Rotation[/h2]
The priority for [color=hunter]Beast Mastery Hunter[/color] is aimed towards keeping powerful spells on cooldown, and filling in the gaps with the less powerful spells. There isn't much in terms of resource management. You work your way down the priority list, and use the more powerful abilities as they become available. Below, we break down the main priority lists for [color=hunter]Beast Mastery Hunter:[/color] your Single-Target Rotation, your AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.
[wrapper width=85%][center][box border=true]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false]Hero Talent Master Switches[/h3]
	[pad]
	You can use the master switches below to flip the [b][i]entire page's[/i][/b] options to your selected choice.

	[center]
		[wrapper width=80%]
		[grid]
			[display-option="pack-leader" checked radio="Hero" icon=inv_ability_packleaderhunter_vicioushunt]Pack Leader[/display-option]
			[display-option="dark-ranger" radio="Hero" icon=inv_ability_darkrangerhunter_blackarrow]Dark Ranger[/display-option]
		[/grid]
		[/wrapper]
	[/center]
[/box][/center][/wrapper]
[br]
[tabs name="Rotations" uniform=true]

[tab name="Single-Target Priority" icon=spell_holy_divinespirit]

sections.heading: Single Target Priority
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Single Target Priority" type=bar][icon name=ability_hunter_bestialdiscipline color=c3 inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] [color=c3] Best Beast Mastery Hunter Single Target Rotation[/color][/h2]
	[pad]
	[color=hunter]Beast Mastery Hunter[/color] in Single-Target plays around a priority list, juggling both ability cooldowns and resources based on an order of power. This means with each GCD we go top to bottom on a list, and press the button with the current highest value.[span display-options="pack-leader"] With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-pack-leader] [color=orange-gem]Pack Leader[/color] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span][span display-options="dark-ranger"] With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-dark-ranger] [color=purple-gem]Dark Ranger[/color] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span]


	[div display-options="!(pack-leader)&!(dark-ranger)"]
	[center][box border=true]
	[b][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-legendary-available] Please select a Hero Talent option to generate a Single Target priority[/b]
	[/box][/center]
	[/div]

[wrapper width=850px]
	[div display-options="pack-leader"]
	[wrapper][center][box border=true][center][small][i]The builds used below are covered in the [url guide=3152]Talents page[/url]. Anywhere you see the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.[/i][/small][/center]
	[/box][/center]
	[/wrapper]
The rotation for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-pack-leader] [color=orange-gem]Pack Leader[/color] aims to primarily play around [spell=1273126] and your tier set, but is otherwise very straightforward.


	[h3 type=bar toc=false]Priority[/h3]
	[ol]

	        [li] Cast [spell=217200] if [spell=19574] is available in the next 3 seconds or about to reach 2 charges.[/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=19574]. [/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=34026] if you have a [spell=471876] buff or [spell=1273126] active. [span class=tip tooltip=KCsave][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] [/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=193455] if you have [spell=1299389] active. [/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=217200]. [/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=193455]. [/li]
	[/ol]


	[/div]

	[div display-options="dark-ranger"]
	[wrapper][center][box border=true][center][small][i]The builds used below are covered in the [url guide=3152]Talents page[/url]. Anywhere you see the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.[/i][/small][/center]
	[/box][/center]
	[/wrapper]
The [symbol=wow-hero-talent-dark-ranger] [color=purple-gem]Dark Ranger[/color] rotation plays around your cooldown window a bit and weaves between [spell=34026]s, [spell=217200]s and [spell=466930]s.


	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c3]Priority[/color][/h3]
	      [ol]
	        [li] Cast [spell=217200] if [spell=19574] is about to come off cooldown in the next 3 seconds. [/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=19574]. [/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=34026] if you have the [spell=1273126] buff active. [span class=tip tooltip=KCsave][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=466930]. [/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=217200]. [/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=392060]. [span class=tip tooltip=WailingArrow][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span]  [/li]
		[li] Cast [spell=193455]. [/li]
		[/ol]



		[center] [toggler id=dark-ranger-ST hidden]Further Details [icon name=ui_profession_blacksmithing size=small type=round color=c3 inline=true][/icon][/toggler][/center]
		[div id=dark-ranger-ST hidden]

[ul]
[li] [spell=392060] can be used in a variety of spots in your cooldown window, as it is available for 15 seconds. Make sure you do not waste other resources when you use it, such as allowing  [spell=34026] to reach 2 charges. Good RNG with [spell=469638] can delay it for quite a bit but you should make sure you always get it off. [/li]
[/ul]

		[li] Cast [spell=19574] as long as [spell=115939] is active. [span class=tip tooltip=BWOpen][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]

[li] Every [spell=466930] you cast will fire a [spell=467911] cone behind its target, applying [spell=466930]s damage-over-time effect. This means you generally want to try and aim [spell=466930]s at enemies near the front of the pack, to ensure maximum cleave.[/li]

sections.heading: Pre-Combat Checks Before any combat happens, Beast Mastery Hunters should make sure to do the following things. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content. Use Hunter's Mark -
sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Checks[/h2]
Before any combat happens, [color=hunter]Beast Mastery Hunters[/color] should make sure to do the following things. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.
[center][wrapper width=800px][box]
[ul]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Use Hunter's Mark - [/b] [color=q0]You want to make sure to apply [spell=259558] to your main target.[/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Cast Misdirection on the tank - [/b] [color=q0] This can also include your pet in solo content. Check the [url guide=3158]UI & Macros page[/url] for ways to set up macros for [spell=34477].[/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Summon or Revive Pet - [/b] [color=q0]You want to make sure your pet is alive and summoned. If not, cast [spell=982] or [spell=67777]. [/color][/li]
li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Check Pet Auto-casts - [/b][color=q0]You want to make sure [spell=16827] / [spell=17253] / [spell=49966] are toggled as auto-casting, and that [spell=61684], [spell=90328] and [spell=2649] are not auto-casting.[/color][/li]
[/ul]
[/box][/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c3][icon name=ability_hunter_bestialdiscipline type=round size=medium inline=true color=c3][/icon] Beast Mastery Hunter Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]

[color=hunter]Beast Mastery Hunter[/color] has one cooldown in [spell=19574], which has a short CD, but is highly impactful. It has a very large amount of effects tied into itself, and both Hero Trees change it in different ways. You will be aiming to play around it as much as possible.

[pad]

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="Bestial Wrath" icon=ability_druid_ferociousbite]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c3] Bestial Wrath [/color][/h3]

[ul]
[li]The most important aspect is that you use [spell=19574] on cooldown, as often as you possibly can. It sounds simple but losing one use loses a lot of damage.[/li]
[li]While there are a lot of talents that interact with [spell=19574], most of them are passive and not worth playing around. [/li]
[li] [spell=1272099] will be applied to the target the pet is currently attacking. If your pet is not attacking anything, you will not get a bleed. [/li]
[li][spell=1273043] will make your [spell=34026] more powerful, indirectly, since there is one additional pet casting it. [/li]
[li]The initial hit of [spell=19574] is fairly large and more importantly, affected by [spell=115939]. When combined with [spell=1273065], this makes every individual additional hit of [spell=19574] trigger their own [spell=115939].[/li]


[li] For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-pack-leader] [color=orange-gem]Pack Leader[/color]: [ul]
[li]You will cause your next [spell=34026] to trigger a [spell=472741] [/li]
[li]This will fire a line of animals 30 yards in front of you. These animals have no height and will not adjust for curves in the terrain. This means they miss very easily.[/li]
[/ul][/li] 
[li] For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-dark-ranger] [color=purple-gem]Dark Ranger[/color]:[ul]
[li]You will gain one [spell=343248].[/li]
[li]You will gain [spell=466990], making your [spell=466930]s more powerful for a short period. [/li]
[li][spell=1264290] summons one [b]Dark Hound[/b]. [ul]
[li]This [b]Dark Hound[/b], will, notably, trigger [spell=1264690], making [spell=34026] notably stronger.[/li]
[li]The [b]Dark Hound[/b] will do a lot of damage and also benefits from [spell=1217524]. This turns [spell=19574] into an AoE burst cooldown.[/li]
[/ul][/li]
[li][spell=1264290] also gives you access to [spell=392060], which can be used both for its large damage and the AoE silence effect.[/li]
[/ul][/li] 

[li]As this is your only form of cooldown, you will want to line up [b]Racial Abilities[/b], [b]Trinkets[/b] (which buff your stats), and [b]Potions[/b] with it. [/li]
[/ul]
[/tab]
[tab name="Trinkets, Potions and Racials" icon=inv_misc_enggizmos_18]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c3] Trinkets, Potions and Racials[/color][/h3]
[ul]
[li]For [b]Trinkets[/b]:[ul]
[li]Any trinket that increases your stats, including [item=270175], [item=273796], [item=159617], [item=250215], [item=273797] and [item=250225] should be used alongside [spell=19574]. [ul]
[/ul]
[/li]
[li]Any trinket that simply does damage, should just be used on cooldown, such as [item=274496] and [item=274497]. [/li]
[li][item=270168] should always be used outside of Bestial Wrath, as it doesn't benefit from it. Ideally, you would line up [item=271887] so that the max stacks overlap with you using the trinket.[/li]

[/ul]
[/li]
[li]For [b]Potions[/b]:[ul]
[li]You should use your potion alongside your [spell=19574]. Note that it needs to be active before the initial hit so that too gets boosted. Macro-ing it to [spell=19574] works for this. [/li]
[li]You should look to use your potions alongside your trinkets or racials, as long as it does not cost you a usage of your potion. [/li]

[/ul]
[/li]
[li]For [b]Racials[/b]:[ul]
[li]Any racial that increases your stats, such as [spell=26297], [spell=274738], [spell=265221] and [spell=20572], should be used alongside [spell=19574]. [/li]
[li]You should look to use your racial alongside your trinkets or potion, as long as it does not cost you a usage of your racial. [/li]
[li]Any other racial should not be used rotationally, you would rather use a [spell=193455]. [/li]


[/ul]
[/li]
[/ul]
[/tab]

[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c3][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c3][/icon] Beast Mastery Hunter Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]

[color=hunter]Beast Mastery Hunter[/color], while simple, has a few tips and tricks that, while not showing up in the rotation above, do net you notable damage increases overall. These are mostly contained in the below two categories.

[pad]

[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Perfecting your cooldown window" icon=ability_druid_ferociousbite]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c3]Perfecting your cooldown window[/color][/h3]

[ul]
[li] As you approach your cooldown window, you should start planning towards having two charges of [spell=34026] available. [ul]
[li] During the cooldown itself, you should aim to spend as many [spell=34026]s as possible, and buff them all with [spell=1273126]. [/li] 
[/ul]
[/li]
[li] Make sure your pet is attacking your current priority target, so that [spell=1272099] lasts its full duration. If your pet is not attacking anything, you do not get a bleed. 
[ul]
[li]Check out the [url guide=3158]UI & Macros page[/url] for pet attack macros.[/li]
[/ul]
[/li]
[li] Any item that boosts your direct damage (such as a potion or a trinket that gives any stat other than) should be active before [spell=19574] strikes the target, so that the initial hit benefits 
[ul]
[li]Macroing them together is fine for this purpose.  [/li]
[/ul]
[/li]
[li] On AoE, make sure that you have [spell=115939] active when you press [spell=19574], so you get a big AoE burst. [/li]  
[li] Since your cooldown is so short, you might get it back towards the end of Mythic+ packs. It might be wise to hold it if you don't anticipate the encounter lasting longer than 12 more seconds. [/li]  

[li] For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-pack-leader] [color=orange-gem]Pack Leader[/color]: [ul]
[li] You should think about where you are standing relative to the enemy as you go into your cooldown window. You should aim to be at a similar height as the enemy, and not too far away.[/li]
[li]If the enemy is about to die, or move, it might be worth delaying your cooldown window slightly, but not by a significant amount.[/li]
[/ul][/li] 

[li] For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-dark-ranger] [color=purple-gem]Dark Ranger[/color]:[ul]

[li]The [b]Dark Hound[/b] with [spell=1217524] causes your cooldown to gain a powerful AoE burst component. Take advantage of this and line it up with important add spawns. [/li]
[li] [spell=392060] is generally flexible in how you use it but you should generally avoid wasting resources while using it, such as [spell=34026] reaching two charges. You should, however, always use it before the effect runs out. You also have the option of taking advantage of the silence effect in Mythic+.[/li]
[/ul] [/li][/ul]



[/tab]
[tab name="Pet Management" icon=ability_hunter_pet_wolf]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c3] Pet Management [/color][/h3]

Pets are notoriously awkward to manage, so this section will cover various tips and tricks to make this task easier and more effective. 

[ul][li]For AoE, it's relatively important that your pet(s) are central in the pack to maximize the amount of targets hit by [spell=115939] and [spell=1264359]. Pets will generally try to attack the back of the mob, so try to move them to target an enemy whose back is towards the middle of the pack. [/li]

[li] The [url guide=3158]UI & Macros page[/url] has various tools to help control your pets better, including a solution to their broken autocast and various pet attack macros. [/li]

[li] Pets like to get stuck a lot! Generally speaking, your best solution to this is either using your pets' "Follow" or "Passive" commands, or swapping between them. Make sure you have these bound to reasonable keys, as each problem may have a different solution. In a worst-case scenario, you will have to dismiss your pet and resummon it. On some encounters, your pet may die from improperly coded AoE, and on others, they may move out of range and despawn.[/li]

[li] Your [spell=34026] and [spell=217200] will cause your pet charge towards the target. This is important to keep in mind when target-swapping, as you will want to make good use of these effectively to minimize your pets' downtime. [/li]

[li] Your pet also has [spell=61684], which you can manually use to move it around quickly. It is set to auto-cast by default, which often wastes it. [/li]

[li] It's worth turning off [spell=90328] auto-cast, as it makes your pet start attacking the enemy slower.[/li]
[/ul]
[/tab]

[/tabs]
[pad]

Our Beast Mastery Hunter guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Beast Mastery Hunter guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page.
[pad]





[tooltip name=WailingArrow]
This will require you standing still. If [spell=19574] is about to expire, make sure to still cast this.
[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=KCsave]
When [spell=19574] is about to come off cooldown you want to try to save so that you have two charges available. If [spell=471876] is about to become available you wanna hold a charge as well.
[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=BWOpen]
While this is your highest priority, you should NOT open with it, as if your pet is not attacking your target, you will not apply [spell=1272099]. See the opener section.
[/tooltip]


[tooltip name=WildThrash]
Make sure your pet is positioned in the center of the enemy pack so that this and [spell=115939] can strike as many enemies as possible. 

Remember that your pet will always try to melee attack its target from the back.
[/tooltip]
